selection_rule: Every statement by an in-scope officeholder quoted in a story published on Nov. 23 or 24, 2026 in the NPR Politics and PBS NewsHour Politics feeds, as read on Nov. 24 in the morning ET, less the stories earlier pages already used, plus every transcript from the fixed transcript sources dated in that window (one was: a White House statement of Nov. 23). One NPR story, "Trump takes credit for Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia, says its good for the economy," could not be read and is not included. Transcripts from Nov. 17 to 22 were searched only to confirm quotes; none held any of the day's quotes. PBS NewsHour carries Associated Press reporting. Seven of the eighteen readable stories quoted no officeholder in scope. Greetings, quotes under five words, commentators' accounts of what officials said, reporters' paraphrases of opinions, and statements by people outside the offices in scope (including an acting Army secretary, the Democratic National Committee chair, a governor-elect, company executives and lawyers) were left out. Statements are worded as the outlet reported them.
lede: Coverage on Nov. 23 and 24 centered on Nvidia's board reinstating chief executive Jensen Huang. President Trump said in a PBS News call and a CNBC interview that he had pressed for the return, and members of both parties in Congress called for hearings and investigations. Sen. Tim Scott announced that Huang will testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3.

Other stories covered Rep. Jimmy Gomez's resignation after a House Ethics Committee report, the coming vote for Senate Democratic leader between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen, the health care plans of congressional Democrats and of the president, the Republican Party after its midterm losses, and the Army's planned detonation of degraded explosive material in Iowa, which Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe addressed.

The page lists 59 statements by 24 officeholders. Nineteen are factual claims or factual premises of predictions; their checks are listed with each statement, and any not yet returned are marked not yet checked. The other 40 are opinions, predictions or promises, listed without a check.

statements.speaker: Barack Obama
statements.office: Former President of the United States
statements.context: Told newly elected congressional Democrats at the Capitol, according to a transcript cited by the AP, about the Affordable Care Act.
statements.topic: Health care agenda for new Congress
statements.quote: But I was very explicit at the time. This is a starter home. It is not the answer
statements.test: True if, around the passage of the Affordable Care Act in 2010, Obama publicly described the law as a first step, a starter home or not the final answer. False if his statements at the time presented it as complete and no such description from then can be found while his later 'starter home' remarks are dated years afterwards. statements.finding: Obama's March 2010 remarks to the House Democratic Caucus, after the House vote and at the signing contain no "starter home", "first step" or "not the answer" wording, though on March 20 he said: "Now, is this bill perfect? Of course not. Will this solve every single problem in our health care system right away? No." The remarks say the law was not a complete solution, but they do not use the explicit framing he describes.

statements.speaker: Elizabeth Warren
statements.context: Wrote in a joint statement with Sen. Jim Banks in November about Nvidia's chip export approvals to China.
statements.quote: Since then, NVIDIA has reportedly received approvals to export hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips to China, including to companies tied to China's military, all while attempting to influence the debate over chip controls in Washington, D.C.
statements.test: True if U.S. export approvals for Nvidia to sell advanced AI chips to China numbering in the hundreds of thousands, including to buyers tied to China's military, are documented by a primary source or credible reporting. False if official records show Nvidia received no such approvals or far fewer. Cannot be determined if the number or recipients of approvals cannot be found.
statements.finding: As reported by The Standard (Hong Kong) from a House Foreign Affairs Committee release, Commerce approved 879,000 Nvidia and AMD chips for Chinese buyers from December 2025 to May 2026, including Tencent, Alibaba and Baidu, which the report says are on the Pentagon's list of Chinese military companies; the Nvidia-only share is not given and the release could not be read directly. AskAmerica's Senate lobbying disclosures show Nvidia filed in-house lobbying reports every quarter of 2025, spending $620,000 to $1.9 million a quarter, with issues including export controls and the Chip Security Act.

statements.speaker: Jimmy Gomez
statements.context: Said in a statement on Nov. 23 after the House Ethics Committee report, about his conduct outside his marriage.
statements.quote: personal mistakes I committed outside of my marriage
statements.test: True if the House Ethics Committee report or Gomez's own statements describe conduct by Gomez outside his marriage. False if the report and record show no such conduct. Cannot be determined if neither the report nor his statement can be read.
statements.finding: The Ethics Committee report records that Gomez was married at the time of the encounter with a House staffer it examined and describes sexual contact with her and a past sexual relationship with a second employee; it also quotes his own reference to mistakes outside his marriage.

statements.quote: Among other significant deficiencies and omissions, the report does not include key portions of my testimony that are essential to a full and fair understanding of what occurred
statements.test: True if the Ethics Committee report omits testimony Gomez gave that bears on the findings. False if the report includes his testimony in full or he gave no testimony. Cannot be determined if the report and the record of his testimony cannot both be read.
statements.finding: The report quotes Gomez's interview testimony on several points but does not reproduce it in full. The interview transcript and the report's exhibits could not be read, so whether omitted testimony bears on the findings could not be determined.

statements.speaker: Jimmy Gomez
statements.context: Wrote in a Nov. 23 statement about how the House Ethics Committee report treated his interview.
statements.quote: In my interview, I answered the Committee's questions only to see my statements selectively quoted, disparaged, and disregarded throughout the final report, to which I was given no opportunity to respond.
statements.test: True if the Ethics Committee report quotes Gomez's interview selectively and he had no opportunity to respond to the final report before release. False if the report shows he was given the draft or final report and an opportunity to respond. Cannot be determined if the report's account of the process cannot be read.
statements.finding: The report's procedural history says the committee interviewed 10 witnesses, including Gomez, and adopted the report on Nov. 19, but it does not say whether he was given a draft or a chance to respond. It quotes parts of his testimony, which by itself does not settle whether the quotation was selective.

statements.speaker: Jimmy Gomez
statements.context: The AP reported what Gomez had said earlier about the House Ethics Committee investigation and his conduct.
statements.quote: Reported as: Gomez had previously said he would cooperate with the investigation but also stressed that his actions were consensual in nature and did not violate the law or House Ethics rules.
statements.test: True if the Ethics Committee report finds Gomez's conduct consensual and finds no violation of the law or House rules. False if the report finds his advances were unwelcome or that he violated House rules. Cannot be determined if the report cannot be read.
statements.finding: The Ethics Committee report determined that Gomez violated clauses 1 and 18(b) of the House Code of Official Conduct by making unwelcome sexual advances toward a staffer, and found his account that the encounter was consensual "not reconcilable" with her testimony, which it judged credible. What remains open: this is a committee finding the House has not acted on; the committee recommended no sanction, and the report says the conduct could implicate D.C. misdemeanor law without any criminal process being under way.

also_said.quote: Gomez denied the interactions were nonconsensual.

statements.test: True if the planned detonation of lead azide in Iowa is carried out and controlled by a federal agency (the Army) rather than a state. False if a state agency directs or conducts it. Cannot be determined if the operator and authority cannot be identified.

statements.quote: Reported as: Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe said state agencies are working to establish additional monitoring of air and water quality, public health and agriculture resources.
statements.test: True if Missouri state agencies have announced or are documented setting up added air, water, health or agriculture monitoring for the detonation.
